title: Ruff
description: Find Python lint violations, common mistakes, and selected security patterns with configurable built-in rules.
markdown: # Ruff ## First try **Illustrative example; not executed in this review.** [Install Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/installation/), then save this as `sample.py`: ```python import math print("Ready") ``` Run this in the directory containing the file. It checks for unused imports without changing the file or loading project configuration: ```sh ruff check --isolated --select F401 sample.py ``` Representative diagnostic excerpt, not captured output (formatting varies by version): ```text sample.py:1:8: F401 `math` imported but unused ``` The location identifies the import; `F401` identifies the unused-import rule. Remove that line and repeat the check. A clean result means this selected rule found no violation in this file. ## Use it on your project Follow the [Ruff tutorial](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/tutorial/) to configure rule selection, file exclusions, and the target Python version. Run `ruff check` for linting; `ruff format` only formats code. Start without automatic fixes so you can inspect the diagnostics. ## Fixes and limitations Ruff distinguishes safe and unsafe fixes. Review proposed changes and run your tests after applying them. Record the tool version, configuration, and preview setting for repeatable results. ## Alternatives and complements Follow the [Ruff and mypy recipe](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/guides/python-checks/) to check one project with separate lint and type reports. Pair Ruff with [mypy](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/mypy/) or [Pyright](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/pyright/) when you also need type checking. Consider [Bandit](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/bandit/) for a dedicated Python security-rule workflow. [Pylint](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/pylint/) uses inference and supports plugins; Ruff provides built-in rule families. Their rules overlap but are not interchangeable. Before switching, compare the diagnostics and plugin requirements of your project. The [official comparison](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/faq/#how-does-ruffs-linter-compare-to-pylint) explains these differences. Use the [finding review workflow](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/guides/reviewing-findings/) to investigate a diagnostic and verify a correction. - **Summary:** Find Python lint violations, common mistakes, and selected security patterns with configurable built-in rules. - **Use it for:** Use Ruff to check Python files for unused imports, common mistakes, and coding conventions. - **What you need:** Python files or supported notebooks and an installed Ruff command. Choose the target Python version and rules for your project. - **What you get:** Diagnostics with a rule code and file location. Some rules offer fixes you can review. - **Checks and limits:** Checks depend on the rules you enable. Security rules need deliberate selection; use a separate type checker for type consistency. - **Finding scope:** Selected lint families; security-related rules require configuration. Ruff is not a Python type checker. ## Compatibility and scope - **Analysis mode:** Static - **What it examines:** Source code - **Context:** Source code, Notebooks - **Techniques:** Linting, Bug finding - **Finding categories:** Logic errors, Coding conventions, Unsafe API use - **Where it runs:** Windows, Linux, and macOS through supported binary distributions or Python packages. - **Languages / ecosystem:** Python - **Language support:** Supported syntax and modernization suggestions depend on the configured Python target version. Notebook rules have additional restrictions. - **Edition and scope:** Ruff's Python linter, including documented notebook support. Formatting is a separate operation. ## Cost and editions - **Cost:** Free - **Cost conditions:** Free open-source linter and formatter, with no paid analyzer edition required. Editor integration and local checks do not require a hosted account. - **License category:** Open source - **License:** MIT, with third-party notices in the project license file Cost information checked 2026-09-22. Runtimes, hosting, and compute may cost extra. Free trials are not counted as free editions. ## Sources and evidence [Official website](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) - [First lint check tutorial](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/tutorial/) - [Installation platforms](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/installation/) - [Ruff overview](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) - [Linter configuration and fix safety](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/linter/) - [File discovery and notebook support](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/configuration/) - [Ruff limitations and comparison with type checkers](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/faq/) - [Ruff license and third-party notices](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/blob/main/LICENSE) Source: [ToolWiki page](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/ruff/). [JSON record and content revision](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/knowledge/v1/documents/tools/ruff.json). - **Documentation reviewed:** 2026-09-22 - **Execution evidence:** not-recorded - **Execution scope:** No structured execution record for this document. Read the text for illustrative examples and limitations. Documentation review is separate from execution evidence. A recorded execution applies only to its stated environment and scope; not-recorded means no structured execution record is supplied.
